title: Build a lead scoring and enrichment agent
description: A system that turns a bare name or email into a verified record and a transparent score with plain-language reasoning.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

hubspot.title: HubSpot
hubspot.content: A CRM and marketing platform used by sales, marketing, and customer success teams. Common target for AI automations — students connect it to draft outreach, enrich contacts, or sync data with other tools.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.content: The event that kicks off an automation, like 'new email received' or 'row added to a sheet.' Every Zapier or n8n workflow starts with a trigger and then runs the actions that follow.

batch-api.title: Batch API
batch-api.content: A way to send a big pile of requests to Claude at once and get the results back later (usually within 24 hours) at a discount. Good for one-time bulk jobs like classifying 10,000 customer support tickets.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

children.text: A new lead lands with a name and an email and not much else. Turning that into a scored, enriched record is one of the clearest wins for AI agents in sales, cleaner than closing a deal or handling an objection. The gap is trust. A score with no visible reasoning gets ignored the first time a rep disagrees with it.

This system runs whenever a new lead enters your pipeline. It pulls what it can verify about the person and company, flags what it can't, and produces a score with a one-line reason per factor, so you see what moved the number.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) for each new lead, a saved [skill](#tooltip-skill), or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that scores a [batch](#tooltip-batch-api) at once. Every version keeps disqualification separate from scoring, so a lead that should be flagged doesn't quietly get buried in a low number.

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming your ICP, your disqualification criteria, your scoring inputs, and where a scored lead should land.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that scores and enriches new leads as they come in. Ask me questions, one at a time, about what a good-fit lead looks like for us, where new leads enter our pipeline, and what should disqualify a lead versus just lower its score. When you have what you need, write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: separating disqualification from scoring up front keeps a bad-fit lead from landing as a low score instead of a clear flag.

items: Which enrichment data your team can already reach, and what needs a new source.
Where a new lead sits before it gets scored.
Who needs to see the reasoning behind a score.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it in a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and ask it to poke holes. Then gather any access it calls for. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are enrichment data (Apollo, Clay, ZoomInfo), your CRM or lead source (Salesforce, [HubSpot](#tooltip-hubspot)), and your sequencing tool to route the high scores. The paste-in version needs none.

**Create.** Start building the system your scope document describes, and test it on a real lead, one you already know the right answer for. The prompt below is an example of the core task. Your scope document will give you a version shaped to your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Score and enrich the attached lead ([name/email]) and explain the score in plain language.

Context: [Paste what you know: name, email, company, role. Also note your ICP, e.g. "series B SaaS, 50 to 200 employees, economic buyer or above," and your scoring inputs, e.g. firmographic fit, engagement, intent signals.]

Rules:
- Output a score plus a one-line reason for each factor that moved it.
- Separate verified data (name the source) from inferred signals.
- Say so plainly if a data point is missing instead of guessing.
- If the lead matches a disqualification criterion, flag it instead of scoring it low: [list your disqualification criteria, e.g. "no budget authority," "outside our supported region"].
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: naming the reason behind every point keeps the score checkable instead of a number a rep has to trust blind.

children.text: **Review.** Check against your scope. Reason per factor, verified separated from inferred, disqualification flagged instead of buried?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what went wrong ("that's inferred, not verified, mark it as such") and fold each correction into the rules.

items: Add a re-scoring [trigger](#tooltip-trigger) when engagement changes.
Report score accuracy against actual conversions.
Flag leads that fit a different rep's territory or vertical.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat draft the rubric and a run log together.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each scored lead, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, lead scored, score given, whether it converted, and what rule I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns make a bad threshold visible once enough leads have run their course.

children.text: **Log** every run against the rubric. Note the date, which checks passed or failed, and what changed. After enough leads convert or don't, it shows which scoring inputs predict a real lead. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the rubric passes a few runs straight, package the prompt and your corrected rules into a reusable AI skill, so every run starts from your defaults. A repeated failure earns its own skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s built-in skill-creator skill will interview you and write it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
One durable failure mode. Unverified data treated as fact quietly degrades a good score into noise, so keep verified and inferred signals visibly separate on every run.
